description: Combine named regex token rules into a single alternation and scan source code into Token tuples with line and column numbers.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `TOKEN_SPEC` lists `(name, pattern)` pairs in priority order. It places `FLOAT` before `INT`, `KEYWORD` (guarded by `\b`) before `IDENT`, and two-character operators (`GE`, `LE`, `EQEQ`, `NE`) before one-character operators (`EQ`, `GT`, `LT`). Line 24 joins all of them into `MASTER` using `"|".join(f"(?P<{name}>{pat})" ...)`.

Look at lines 10-14 and 22: Python's `|` alternation picks the first branch that matches at the current index. Placing `KEYWORD` before `IDENT` makes `while` a `KEYWORD`; placing `LE` before `LT` and `EQ` makes `<=` a single `LE` token. `MISMATCH` (`r"."`) at the very bottom catches any unrecognized character.

`tokenize(source)` iterates over `MASTER.finditer(source)`, reading `kind = m.lastgroup` and `lexeme = m.group()`. It computes `col = m.start() - line_start + 1`. On `"NEWLINE"`, it increments `line` and resets `line_start = m.end()`. It skips `"SKIP"` and `"COMMENT"`, raises `SyntaxError` on `"MISMATCH"`, and yields `Token(kind, lexeme, line, col)` for everything else.
Lines 46-54 run `tokenize(code)` on a 5-line program containing a `# initialize` comment, a `while (count2 <= 10)` loop, and `print count2;`.

steps.answer: `# initialize` matches `COMMENT` and is skipped by `continue` on line 35. `\n` matches `NEWLINE` and sets `line = 2` and `line_start = m.end()` on line 33. Thus, `while` is yielded as `Token(type='KEYWORD', lexeme='while', line=2, col=1)`.
steps.question: When `MASTER.finditer(code)` scans line 1 (`let count2 = 0;   # initialize\n`), what happens to `# initialize` and `\n`, and what are `line` and `col` for the next token `while` on line 47?

steps.description: After scanning `# initialize` at the end of line 1, `kind == "NEWLINE"` triggers line 33. It increments `line` to `2` and sets `line_start = 31`.

title: A Master-Regex Lexer with Priority Ordering and Line Tracking
